summary: Quickstart templates: customer confusion about 429 handling (Retry-After/backoff) and wants clearer docs + sample code
description:
Customer (Devkit AI) is using the new Quickstart templates as their primary onboarding path and is confused about how to handle HTTP 429 responses from the Redwood Hosted API.

Issue summary:
- Customer followed the TypeScript agents template and saw intermittent 429s under light load (local dev + a small proxy in front).
- They were unsure whether to implement their own retry/backoff, rely on the SDK, or treat 429 as a hard failure.
- They did not understand whether to use the Retry-After header (seconds vs ms), or how to handle rate-limit bursts safely without creating retry storms.
- The template README currently mentions “retries/backoff” but does not show a complete example covering:
  - honoring Retry-After
  - exponential backoff with jitter
  - max retry cap and overall request timeout budget
  - differentiating 429 vs 5xx vs timeouts
  - idempotency guidance (avoid re-running non-idempotent tool calls)

Impact:
- Increased support load: customer opened multiple questions in chat/email asking for a canonical approach.
- Risk of poor production patterns: customer attempted immediate retry loops and increased concurrency, which can amplify throttling.

Environment:
- Hosted API: prod (us-east)
- Template: TypeScript agents template (Node)
- Customer was calling a chat completion endpoint with streaming enabled.

Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1) Start template app locally.
2) Set high parallelism in their own wrapper (e.g., 20 concurrent requests) to test.
3) Observe some requests failing with HTTP 429.
4) Add naïve retry loop; observe continued 429s and occasional long tail latency.

Observed behavior:
- HTTP 429 with error payload indicating rate limit / quota exceeded.
- Customer did not see a clear path in template docs on how to retry safely, what limits to expect, and how to debug using Console.

Expected behavior:
- Templates should show a “blessed” snippet for 429 handling (including Retry-After) and reference SDK defaults.
- Docs should explicitly state what the SDK does by default for retries/timeouts (streaming vs non-streaming).

Requested outcome:
- Update quickstart template docs with a copy/paste-safe backoff example.
- Clarify when not to retry (e.g., invalid API key, invalid request) and when to reduce concurrency.
- Add a short troubleshooting section: how to find 429s in Console (route/model breakdown) and correlate request_id.

Notes:
- This appears related to other post-launch questions (SUP-2934 streaming/proxy) but the core ask here is clarity + sample code for 429/backoff behavior.
comments: 2026-02-16 09:42 Dev Patel (Support): Logging ticket based on Devkit AI email + in-app chat. They’re using the TS agent quickstart and asked for “the official way” to handle 429. They specifically asked whether we guarantee Retry-After header and whether SDK already retries 429.

2026-02-16 10:05 Owen Phillips (Support): Replied to customer acknowledging the confusion and asked for: SDK version, template commit/tag, whether they’re using streaming, and whether they’re behind a proxy/load balancer. Set expectations that 429 should be handled with backoff + jitter and that we’ll provide a canonical snippet.

2026-02-16 11:18 Customer (Devkit AI): Confirmed streaming is enabled. They added their own retry loop because template README only says “handle 429s gracefully.” They’re on redwood-sdk-typescript ~0.9.x (exact version not pinned) and copied the quickstart about a week ago. They asked if Retry-After is “ms or seconds” and whether they should retry indefinitely.

2026-02-16 12:02 Monica Patel (SDK Lead): SDK behavior clarification: current TS SDK retries some transient network errors; 429 handling is present but not obvious in docs and streaming has different retry semantics (don’t blindly restart stream without a bounded budget). Recommended: honor Retry-After if present, otherwise use exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter; cap retries and enforce overall timeout budget. Also recommend emitting attempt count + final status to logs/metrics to avoid silent loops.

2026-02-16 13:10 Sean Gallagher (SRE): Suggested doc language: treat 429 as a signal to reduce concurrency and/or request rate. Default guidance: max 3–5 retries, jitter required, and respect Retry-After. Do not set a default that can hammer the API (no “retry forever”). Also mention 429s can occur even under low load if multiple processes share the same API key or if a proxy is retrying upstream.

2026-02-17 09:25 Wei Chen (Docs): Proposed doc update: add a dedicated “Handling 429 / rate limits” section to each quickstart (RAG + agents + combined) with the same snippet and explanation. Include: Retry-After units (seconds) and a note that some proxies can strip headers; show log fields to include (request_id, attempt, backoff_ms).

2026-02-17 14:40 Elliot Price (Docs Lead): Approved adding a single canonical snippet linked from each template README to avoid drift. Also requested we add a small “anti-patterns” callout: immediate retry loops, retrying non-idempotent tool actions, increasing concurrency when you see 429.

2026-02-18 11:05 Support (Owen Phillips): Sent interim guidance to customer: backoff + jitter, cap retries, honor Retry-After (seconds), and reduce concurrency. Shared link to SDK retry/timeout recommendations page and asked them to pin SDK version and template tag to reduce confusion.

2026-02-19 16:22 Wei Chen (Docs): Docs PR merged to clarify 429 handling and add sample backoff code (TS + Python). Also aligned template README wording to explicitly state what the SDK does by default vs what the app should implement at the request layer. Linked changes to redwood-docs/pr-889 and quickstart papercut cleanup in redwood-quickstarts/pr-402.

2026-02-20 09:03 Dev Patel (Support): Confirmed with customer: they can now follow the updated section; they removed their infinite retry loop, pinned concurrency, and 429s dropped to near-zero. Closing ticket.
resolution: Updated quickstart template documentation to include a canonical, copy/paste-safe 429 handling pattern (honor Retry-After in seconds, exponential backoff with jitter, bounded retries, and overall timeout budget) and clarified SDK default retry/timeout behavior for streaming vs non-streaming. Template README wording updated to reduce ambiguity and point to the shared docs section.
next_steps: Add a short “Rate limit troubleshooting in Console” subsection (filter 429 by route/model; correlate request_id) in next docs patch, and ensure templates log attempt/backoff fields consistently with telemetry contract v1.
